dialogs.api_keys.intro: Enter the API Key for at least one provider (Groq and Google Gemini offer an instant free tier). Your keys travel straight from your PC to the official provider with zero intermediary servers.
dialogs.api_keys.ram_only_chk: ⚡ Ephemeral Mode (RAM Only — Do not save to disk)
dialogs.api_keys.ram_only_tip: When enabled, keys live only in RAM while the game is open and are destroyed when the window closes.
dialogs.api_keys.provider_desc.deepseek: Ultra-affordable with 90% prefix caching and great narrative quality.
dialogs.api_keys.provider_desc.groq: Instant speed with 8,000 TPM on the free tier: enough for campaign creation and playing in compact mode.
dialogs.api_keys.provider_desc.router: Unified access to hundreds of models (including :free tier models).
dialogs.api_keys.provider_desc.gemini: Gemini 2.5 Flash models with a huge context window and generous free tier.
dialogs.api_keys.groq_tpm_notice: ⚠️ Honesty note about free Groq: the limit is 8,000 TPM (input + reserved output). Campaign creation usually fits, but gameplay turns send a compact prompt (abbreviated rules) to stay under the cap and prose may be somewhat briefer. If a heavy turn exceeds it, add Gemini or DeepSeek too: they don't have that cap.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The engine blocks at the code level sending Authorization headers to any domain outside:
{hosts}

🔍 HOW TO VERIFY IT YOURSELF IN 15 SECONDS:
1. Open Windows Resource Monitor (resmon.exe -> Network tab -> Processes with Network Activity).
2. Run a game turn and observe that the only outgoing TCP connection goes to the official IP

3. In the public GitHub repository you can inspect 'src/core/credentials.py' and 'src/llm/gateway.py'
   and compare this binary's SHA-256 hash against the one built by GitHub Actions.

dialogs.community.share_window_title: 🧪 Help Improve the Engine — Share Chronicle & Logs
dialogs.community.share_header: 🧪 WANT TO HELP ME IMPROVE THIS?
dialogs.community.share_banner_html:
I'm building this engine solo, and the most helpful thing for tuning it is seeing how it behaves in real runs: when the DM narrates well, when it hallucinates, or when rules slip.

If you'd like to help, you can send me your playthrough (it is completely optional). The button below packs your save and logs into a .zip, scrubbing your API Keys and your PC username first. It also opens the folder so you can inspect the .zip yourself before sending.
dialogs.community.rating_5: 5/5 - Worked great, the DM nailed it
dialogs.community.rating_4: 4/5 - Very good, only a couple of weird quirks
dialogs.community.rating_3: 3/5 - Playable, though the DM or rules slipped
dialogs.community.share_notes_label: 💬 Tell me briefly how it went or what felt off (Optional):
dialogs.community.share_notes_ph: E.g. 'On turn 8 it handled a wild stunt cleanly, but on turn 12 the goblin came back to life...' or simply 'Sending my save so you can see how the run went.'
